notes: Text-to-3D, coding-agent setting. Parity subset: 50 of the 212 tasks drawn at random (random.Random(0) for the first 20, random.Random(1) for 30 more from the rest; `--split parity`, listed in src/threedcodebench/parity.py). Both sides ran Codex CLI 0.171.0 with gpt-5.4-mini (model-default reasoning) through the same OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with the upstream prompt and a 600 s agent budget; the original side ran upstream's tasks/coding_agent/run_codex_agent.sh unchanged except for the Blender path. Metrics are the four Table 2 metrics: executability over all tasks, and SigLIP-2 text-image, Uni3D 3D-3D and Chamfer distance (cd_yawmin, lower is better) as conditional means over tasks with a value. Executability, Uni3D and Chamfer run-score ranges overlap. SigLIP-2 ranges do not (original 0.1406-0.1418, Harbor 0.1438-0.1476); the README documents the investigation: the two scorers give the same SigLIP-2 on the same scripts (all 300 scripts cross-scored both ways, mean difference below 1e-4), Codex sends identical API requests on both sides apart from the working-directory path, and the paired per-task difference is +0.0045 with SE 0.0041 (p = 0.27). One Harbor trial (leafheart-seed0, run 2) hit AgentSetupTimeoutError before the agent started and was re-run with `harbor jobs resume -f AgentSetupTimeoutError`. Each run was executed as two jobs (20 + 30 tasks) because the subset was extended from 20 to 50 tasks. Parity and oracle artifacts (all attempts, aggregation scripts) are in a personal HF dataset while the shared parity-experiments repo is over its file limit (adapters#129), pinned at commit 71bb3917ccfb993c188dd75050c1d7274d0aa09f; its SHA256SUMS (11,798 files) has SHA-256 12d7cef3f411205913c272b2777e3e14e579a656813bb4272f7102717351f51e.

metrics.metric: chamfer_distance cd_yawmin (conditional mean, lower is better)
